terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. `node src/orders.ts` runs the orders, and `npm run types` checks their types.

tasks.title: Type an order line
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/orders.ts`, give the parameter of `lineGrams` the type of an order line: an object with `tins` (a number) and `gramsPerTin` (a number). Write its result type too. Leave its body as it is.

Check reads your function for the result type. It compiles calls of its own: an order line, and a whole line that has a blend as well, must compile, while a line without its grams per tin, tins as text, a number on its own or a result used as text must be refused. It calls `lineGrams` with lines of its own.
nextSteps: Run `npm run types` and read the error for the parameter of `lineGrams`.
Write an object type after the parameter: curly braces, and each property with its type.
Write the result type after the round brackets.
hints: An object type looks like an object, with a type where each value would be.
Inside the curly braces, write each property's name, a colon and its type, with a semicolon between them.
`export function lineGrams(line: { tins: number; gramsPerTin: number }): number {`.

tasks.title: Let the gift note be missing
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, the compiler refuses the call to `slipText` for an order with no gift note. Read why, then change the type of the parameter so a gift note may be left out. Then make `slipText` give back just `'Order OK-1043'` for an order without a note, and `'Order OK-1042, note: ...'` with the note for an order that has one.

Check compiles calls of its own: with and without a note must compile, while an order without an id, a note that is a number or a slip used as a number must be refused. It calls `slipText` with orders of its own, with a note and without.
nextSteps: Run `npm run types` and read the error for the second call, and the note under it.
Mark the gift note in the type as a property an order may leave out.
Run `node src/orders.ts`: what does the second slip say now?
Make the body give back only the order part when there is no note.
hints: `Property 'giftNote' is missing in type ... but required in type ...` means the object passed has no `giftNote`, and the type says every order must have one.
A question mark after a property's name in a type makes it optional. Reading it then gives `undefined` when it is missing, and the compiler knows that.
Write `giftNote?: string` in the type, and in the body `if (order.giftNote === undefined) return `Order ${order.id}`` before the line with the note.

tasks.title: Keep the order id fixed
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, a line changes the id of `firstOrder`, and the compiler says nothing. Change the type of `firstOrder` so its `id` can never change, while its `tins` still can. Read what the compiler says then, and remove the line it points at.

Check compiles code of its own: reading the id and changing the tins must compile, while giving the order a new id or tins as text must be refused. It reads `firstOrder` after your lines.
nextSteps: Run `node src/orders.ts`: which id does the first order end with?
Mark `id` in the type of `firstOrder` as a property that cannot be changed.
Run `npm run types` and read the error it gives for the line that changes the id.
Remove that line, keep the one that changes the tins, and run both commands.
hints: `const` keeps the name `firstOrder` from pointing at another object, but it does not stop the properties of that object from changing.
The word `readonly` in front of a property in a type means it can be set when the object is made, and never after.
The type becomes `{ readonly id: string; tins: number }`, and the line `firstOrder.id = 'OK-1043'` goes.

tasks.title: Write the parcel function whole
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, write a function called `parcelFor`, with `export` in front, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It takes an order id (text) and the grams in the parcel (a number). It gives back an object with three properties: `orderId`, the id; `grams`, the grams; and `heavy`, `true` when the parcel weighs more than 2000 g. Write the result type as an object type, then take away the `//` in front of the line that prints it.

Check reads your function for its result type. It compiles code of its own that reads the three properties as text, a number and true or false, which must compile, and code that reads a property a parcel does not have or uses one as the wrong type, which must be refused. It calls `parcelFor` with parcels of its own.
nextSteps: Write the first line: the name, two typed parameters and an object type as the result type.
Give back an object with the three properties.
Take away the `//` in front of the line under it.
Run both commands, and try a heavy parcel on the line.
hints: A result type can be an object type, written the same way as a parameter's.
The result type names `orderId`, `grams` and `heavy` with their types. In the body, `heavy` is a comparison.
It starts `export function parcelFor(orderId: string, grams: number): { orderId: string; grams: number; heavy: boolean } {`.
